question.problem:
A continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}, & 1<x\le 2, \\ \frac{x}{5}, & 2\le x<3.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ with probability density function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\int }_{S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

So, we compute the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot \frac{x}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}\frac{{x}^{3}}{5}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x\,{|}_{1}^{2}+{\frac{{x}^{4}}{20}|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =(2-1)+(\frac{81}{20}-\frac{16}{20}) \\  & =1+\frac{13}{4} \\  & =\frac{17}{4}\end{aligned}
$$
